bbscg.ui.keys.snap_bypass: Hold to drag the timeline off the tick grid
bbscg.ui.reveal_limb_picker_tooltip: Unfold the bone list (the same one the pose keyframes' panel shows) — pick any bone to bring its track in, for limbs the viewport can't click
bbscombinedgizmo.config.title: Keyframe Optimization
bbscombinedgizmo.config.general.title: Keyframe optimizations
bbscombinedgizmo.config.general.tooltip: Gizmo display modes, timeline dragging and keyframe editing tweaks
bbscombinedgizmo.config.general.show_pla: Show two-axis planes in single modes

Whether a single display mode (move only / scale only) also shows the three two-axis planes next to the axis bars — the ones you hold to drag in a plane in any direction. Turn this off for axis bars only; the combined mode always keeps its stock 2.7 look
bbscombinedgizmo.config.general.fraction: Hold a key to drag the timeline off the tick grid

While held, the bound key (left Alt by default, rebindable in the keybind settings) makes timeline drags — the playhead and keyframes alike — keep their fractional time instead of snapping to whole ticks. The same temporary bypass Shift already gives, but on a rebindable key of its own. Stock behaviour when off or not held
bbscombinedgizmo.config.general.auto_key: While editing model keyframes in the replay editor: clicking a limb no longer snaps the timeline to that limb's nearest keyframe — it stays where you left it — and dragging a limb's position or rotation keys the limb at the current timeline position instead (a keyframe is created there from the interpolated pose if none exists yet). Only applies to pose and limb tracks; everything else keeps stock behaviour
bbscombinedgizmo.config.general.summary_: While on, every model's whole-pose track in the replay editor gets a Blender-style summary row right above it: one dot per distinct tick of every visible track at or below the pose row. Clicking a dot selects that whole column of keyframes and dragging it moves them together; clicking the summary row's label (or Ctrl-clicking its lane) creates a keyframe on the pose row beneath. Folded-away tracks take no part in the summary
bbscombinedgizmo.config.general.keyframe: While on, box-selecting one or more limb (or transform) keyframes and right-clicking offers "Flip X/Y/Z axis" at the bottom of the menu: every selected keyframe's value is mirrored across that axis's plane — the translation's axis component flips its sign, the rotation keeps its axis euler angle and negates the other two (the same convention Blockbench's keyframe flip uses), the scale is untouched. Flipping several tracks at once undoes as a single step
bbscombinedgizmo.config.general.batch_ed: While on, box-selecting two or more keyframes makes every value edit from the editor panel and the gizmo — the pose panels' reset buttons included — apply to the whole selection of matching tracks at once, instead of being redirected by auto-keyframing onto a fresh keyframe at the playhead. A single selected keyframe keeps stock behaviour. Numeric edits move each keyframe by the same delta (their spread is kept); pose and other complex values are copied over wholesale
bbscombinedgizmo.config.general.reveal_l: While on, a pose track's limb tracks start hidden once expanded, and they no longer nest in the model's bone hierarchy — they all flatten out right under the pose row: clicking a limb in the viewport reveals its track, and the revealed tracks line up in the order their limbs were clicked; collapsing the pose track resets them to hidden. With a limb keyframe selected, a button at the top of its fields panel opens the bone hierarchy picker (the same searchable one the pose keyframes' panel uses) — picking a bone reveals its track, which reaches limbs the viewport can't click. Revealed tracks stay revealed across undo/redo; switching to another replay starts fresh. Shift-clicking the fold toggle still shows every limb track (flattened too). Turning the setting off brings the stock tree back
bbscombinedgizmo.config.general.snowstor: While on, BBS's Bedrock particle engine understands everything Snowstorm can export: the bezier and bezier_chain curve types (stock degrades them to linear), the lookat_direction and emitter_transform_xy/xz/yz billboard facing modes plus the 'custom' direction mode (stock degrades them to rotate_xyz / derive-from-velocity), gradient ranges beyond 0..1 (stock freezes long gradients mid-way), the whole event system — particle_effect.events with expression / sound / particle-effect payloads, sequence and randomize, emitter and particle creation / expiration / timeline / travel-distance triggers, and collision events — and the manual (emitter_rate_manual) rate mode. Sub emitters spawn at the event's position and don't spawn further sub emitters, so event chains can't explode. Files imported while this is off keep stock behaviour until re-imported; turning it off restores stock 2.7 behaviour
